theory.title: Vocabulary Expander
theory.intro: IELTS Reading demands recognition of 3,000-5,000 academic words beyond everyday English. Most candidates fail not because they can't read, but because they encounter lexical gaps—critical vocabulary they've never seen in context.
theory.trap1Desc: Academic words have multiple meanings. Knowing one definition doesn't transfer to others.
theory.trap2Desc: Words combine in predictable patterns. Native speakers use authentic collocations that memorization alone won't teach.
theory.trap3Desc: Academic vocabulary has formal register. Knowing synonyms doesn't always help with specific academic usage.
theory.solutionIntro: This module uses the method that actually works: encountering words in authentic IELTS-style sentences, not isolated definitions.
theory.step1Desc: You see the word in a real IELTS sentence first, forcing your brain to infer meaning from context.
theory.step2Desc: After inference, you get the exact definition PLUS related forms to build recognition of the entire word family.
theory.step3Desc: You learn common word partnerships. This is how natives recognize words instantly.
theory.step4Desc: Words resurface at optimal intervals. Your brain builds long-term memory through strategic review.
theory.listIntro: We've analyzed 10+ years of IELTS Reading tests to identify the 500 words with the highest ROI.
theory.strategyDesc: Optimal retention comes from learning 10 new words per day while reviewing previous words through spaced repetition.
theory.trap1Example: IELTS Example: "The study addresses the reproducibility crisis" ≠ "Write your address on the form"
theory.trap2Example: Common IELTS Collocations: mitigate risk, exert influence, establish precedent, yield results
theory.trap3Example: Register Shift: show → demonstrate | worsen → exacerbate | lessen → mitigate
theory.step1Inference: Your brain infers: "exacerbate" = make worse (from "amplify" and "instability")
theory.timelineResult: Result after 50 days: 500 words in long-term memory with 90%+ retention rate
theory.ctaDesc: Switch to Practice to start learning the first 50 words through contextual flashcards, or try Battle Mode to test recognition in authentic IELTS passages.

practice.proTip: 💡 Pro Tip: Don't just memorize definitions. Pay attention to collocations and how the word is used in context. This is how you'll recognize it in IELTS passages.

theory.intro: Welcome to the ultimate proving ground for your IELTS Reading preparation. This module features 10 complete practice tests, each mirroring the actual IELTS Academic Reading exam.

theory.timeManagementDesc: Practice maintaining focus and pacing across the full 60-minute duration.
theory.staminaDesc: Train your cognitive endurance to stay sharp through Passage 3.
theory.performanceDesc: Identify patterns in your mistakes and track improvement over time.
theory.minutesDesc: Strict time limit with countdown timer
theory.howToUse: How to Use Mock Tests Effectively
theory.phase1Desc: Take your first mock test with zero preparation to establish your baseline.
theory.phase2Desc: After identifying weaknesses, focus on specific modules before returning to mock tests.
theory.phase3Desc: Ramp up frequency and focus on exam-day readiness.
theory.phase4Desc: Perfect your exam-day routine in the final week.
theory.pitfalls: Common Mock Test Mistakes to Avoid
theory.backToBackDesc: Allow 2-3 days between tests for proper review and recovery.
theory.skippingReviewDesc: Spend at least 30 minutes analyzing each test.

breaks.title: Time for a Brain Break!
breaks.contentFocus: You've been focusing for {{count}} minutes—excellent work!
breaks.contentResearch: Research shows taking a {{count}}-minute break now will boost your retention and refresh your attention.
breaks.footnote: 💡 You can adjust break reminders in Settings
breaks.onBreakText: Great work! Stand up, stretch, grab water, or look away from the screen.
breaks.tipLookAway: 👀 Look at something 20+ feet away (20-20-20 rule)
facts: Your brain consolidates learning during breaks, making them essential for memory formation.
Research shows taking a 5-minute break improves focus by up to 13% in the next session.
The prefrontal cortex (focus control center) needs periodic rest to maintain peak performance.
Teens and young adults maintain optimal attention for 20-40 minutes before needing a cognitive reset.
Taking breaks prevents mental fatigue and actually speeds up overall learning time.
